newsitem.title: UK: GUS profits marginally ahead in current year.
newsitem.headline: GUS profits marginally ahead in current year.

text.p: Britain's biggest home shopping group Great Universal Stores Plc on Thursday reported nearly a two percent drop in profits for last year, but said its performance since then had improved.
The retailer, best known for its exclusive Burberry range of clothing, said profits in the first two months of its current financial year were "marginally in excess" of the same period last year.

Underlying profits, stripping out 21.5 million pounds ($35.8 million) in tax and other credits, plus profits from property disposals, fell more steeply to 549.1 million stg, from 562.3 million in the previous year.
GUS, which has extensive retailing operations overseas, also said the impact of sterling on its overseas earnings reduced group pretax profit by 21.7 million pounds.
The group's biggest division, home shopping, saw profits slip to 124.4 million pounds, from 145.9 million pounds, due to falling sales and the cost of improving service and delivery.
Burberrys profits also dropped to 61.7 million pounds from 62.8 million, hurt by the strength of the pound.

The results mark the first drop in GUS's annual profits in almost half a century. Under the chairmanship of Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale, who took over last summer, the group has begun to try and stem the decline in mail order as well as make acquisitions.

Last year, in a break with its conservative past, GUS embarked on an acquisition spree buying U.S. credit information services company Experian and more recently set up a property joint venture with British Land Plc. ($ = 0.601 British Pounds)
